chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not unjust to His servants, nor does He single out anyone for blessing except by right, or by a good deed, or by patience upon a trial. Indeed, Allah tests the servant with what is disliked to multiply his good deeds, or to raise his ranks, or to expiate his sins. So if he is patient, he is grateful; if he is ignorant, he disbelieves; and if he knows and is patient, he is grateful. That is what Allah, the Exalted, says: 'Verily, the patient will be given their reward without measure.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between patience with knowledge and patience with ignorance in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this hadith within the Imami theological framework, emphasizing that true *balā'* (trial) serves as a mechanism for distinguishing the sincere from the hypocritical. The text highlights that while patience (*sabr*) is the immediate response, it must be coupled with gnosis (*ma'rifah*) to transform suffering into gratitude (*shukr*), thereby preventing the slide into disbelief (*kufr*). This distinction underscores the Shia emphasis on the interplay between action and inner knowledge in achieving spiritual elevation.
